steps.note: Confirm the page came out clean: `meta get` under `--no-config` reads the page alone, and citations is unset.
With the config governing the run, `meta get` reads the merged view, which carries the entry.
Check exactly as before: a fourth column names the manifest and the line the entry starts on.
A half-moved page has two owners for one key: an error naming the manifest and the collection.
`add` needs no flag: the entry goes to the manifest, and the claim stays at the line typed.
`update` writes each manifest once per run, however many entries it repaired.
The page that carries `slug: guide-one` owns the `join:`-keyed entry.

scaffolding: The page's example repository: manni.config.yaml declares the `site` collection (docs/**/*.md, manifest docs-citations.yaml) and the `guides` collection (guides/**/*.md, manifest guides-citations.yaml joined on `slug`).

docs/ holds limits.md, retries.md, moved.md, moved-two.md, own.md (still carries its own citations) and entry-invalid.md (its manifest entry has a malformed integrity); guides/guide.md carries `slug: guide-one`; lib/ holds limits.ts and moved.ts (lines shifted by two).
The refusals need configs the repo doesn't have (a URL manifest; two owning collections), so a spec writes them.
